title: AWS Step Functions Orchestration
summary: Coordinate multi-step workflows with retries, error handling, waits and massive parallelism.
tldr: **Step Functions** runs a state machine: sequence, branch (`Choice`), wait, run in parallel and handle errors, with a visual history of every execution. It replaces Lambda functions that call each other or sleep.

**Standard** workflows run up to a year, are exactly-once and are billed per state transition. **Express** workflows run up to 5 minutes, are at-least-once (async) and are billed per execution, duration and memory.
**Distributed Map** fans out over millions of S3 objects or rows of a large CSV/JSON file as child executions, with a tolerated failure percentage or count.

keyFacts.text: Maximum duration of a **Standard** execution, which makes human approval steps and long waits possible. Express workflows stop at 5 minutes.
The `.waitForTaskToken` pattern pauses a Standard workflow until an external system (approval portal, partner) returns the token with `SendTaskSuccess`.
`Retry` sets `IntervalSeconds`, `MaxAttempts` and `BackoffRate` per error name. `Catch` routes remaining errors to a fallback state, such as a compensation step.
Parallel child executions a **Distributed Map** runs when you leave `MaxConcurrency` unset. Items come straight from an S3 prefix or a large file.
A Standard workflow is billed per state transition, so a `Wait` state isn't billed for the time it waits, unlike a sleeping Lambda function.

traps: Express workflows can't run past 5 minutes and don't support `.waitForTaskToken` or `.sync`, so they can't wait for a human.
Chaining Lambda functions that invoke each other, or one Lambda that sleeps, is costly and fragile compared with a state machine.
An **inline** Map takes its items from the execution input, which has a size limit. Huge item lists need Distributed Map reading from S3.
Switching from Standard to Express does not add automatic retries. Retries come from the `Retry` field.
Moving a polling loop to Express doesn't help when jobs take longer than 5 minutes.
The workflow type can't be changed after the state machine is created; you create a new one.
